newsitem.title: CHINA: China oil firm says no plans to move disputed rig.
newsitem.headline: China oil firm says no plans to move disputed rig.

text.p: China's main offshore oil company said on Thursday it had no plans to move a drilling rig operating in a disputed area off the coast of central Vietnam.
"Any decision to leave the drilling area would be based on the drilling results," an official of the China National Offshore Oil Corp told Reuters.
"Why should we leave the area?" said the official. "When the exploration is finished we will move the rig."

Hanoi has called for immediate and unconditional meetings to resolve a territorial row sparked by China's decision to position the Kan Tan 111 exploration rig in disputed waters between the two countries.
Beijing said on Tuesday it was considering suggestions from Hanoi in the row, but gave no details of its plans for the rig.
The oil exploration dispute is the latest in a series of territorial disputes between the two communist neighbours, which fought a brief but bloody border war in 1979 and clashed at sea in the 1980s.
